The code comment is wrong. Setting sum(r^2) = 0.64 gives a total circle area of pi*0.64 ≈ 2.01, not 64% coverage, because the pi factor is missing. Each starting radius is about 0.157 (sum about 4.1), so the starting circles overlap heavily. SLSQP and the repair step still give a valid packing, so the result is not invalidated, but the starting point is probably not what was intended. A target of 0.64/pi was likely meant.
np.clip to 0.3 happens before rescaling, so after scaling some radii can exceed 0.3 and even 0.5. This is harmless because the optimizer and repair step handle it.
Removing INIT_RADIUS did not break anything: the run finished and was not flagged.

This matches the harness value of -0.584; the small difference is from rounding. The gap is within noise, so rejecting is correct.
